title: Copwax
summary: Copwax is a Rockaway Neck creek name recorded by Tooker. It appears in colonial land-paper context and is related to the earlier Coekwas spelling.
address_label: Rockaway Neck, Queens, NY (approximate general location)
map_geometry_source: Copwax is identified as a creek on Rockaway Neck. Exact creek identification is unresolved; point is a general Rockaway Neck marker offset within the already mapped Rockaway area, not an exact historic coordinate.
translation_content:
Recorded forms include Copwax, Coekwas, Hapax, and Oppeax. Copwax is connected with Copiag and Copeces and interprets it as a shut-in or sheltered place, possibly a canoe shelter. Hapax is interpreted separately as flooded or overflowed land, probably from the meadows bordering the creek.

Why Place Names Matter

“Place names can teach us of the deeper histories of the places we live, work and play.”

— Bonnie McGill, Offensive Names Should Be Removed from Public Lands (2021), Conclusion
land_loss_content: Copwax preserves a creek name from Rockaway Neck within colonial land records. Keeping the name visible alongside broader Rockaway territory records helps distinguish a specific water-place from larger tribal and land-sale histories.
whereintheworld_content: Tooker associates Copwax with Rockaway Neck, but the specific historic creek has not been identified.

source_list.title: William Wallace Tooker, Indian Place-Names on Long Island and Islands Adjacent

source_list.citation: William Wallace Tooker, Indian Place-Names on Long Island and Islands Adjacent (New York and London: G. P. Putnam's Sons, 1911), pp. 81-82.
source_list.citation_context: Tooker entries 60, 72, 97, and 267 for the Rockaway Neck creek-name cluster Coekwas/Copwax/Hapax/Oppeax. Entry 97 interprets Hapax as flooded or overflowed land and says see Coekwas and Oppeax. Entry 267 gives Oppeax as a Rockaway Neck creek and says see Hapax.
